Set-up guide · Route C

Your child has an Android phone, and you have an Android or iPhone

Google's Family Link works whichever phone you have, including an iPhone. Your child's phone needs to be an Android.

Generated from one source. This page, the Word document and the Figma boards are all built from content/guidance.js. The phone screens are drawn, not screenshots. They follow your iOS screenshots, so they stay sharp at any size and can be updated by changing a word.

Every screen is also a separate SVG in assets/guides/screens/. Drop one into Figma and its text stays editable.

What we're asking you to do: spend about 30 to 40 minutes setting up a small number of settings on your child's phone, then leave them running.

Everything you need is already built into the phone. There is nothing to buy, nothing to download, and no separate app to learn.

Start here: find your child's phone, sit down with it for 40 minutes, and work through the one route below that matches your situation.

Before you start: three things to have ready

  • Your child's phone, physically in your hands. You'll need it for part of this, even if you manage it from your own phone afterwards.
  • The password for the account on your child's phone: their Apple Account password (iPhone) or their Google Account password (Android). If your child set the phone up themselves, they will know it and you may not. Ask for it now rather than halfway through.
  • Somewhere to write down a new passcode. You are about to create a four-digit code that locks these settings. If you forget it, you may need to erase the phone completely. Write it where you keep other passwords, not in a note on your child's phone.
! WarningDon't use your child's birthday, your PIN, or a code your child already knows. The settings only hold if the code does.

If your child has more than one device, such as an old or second phone, do the main phone first and tell us about the others at smartphonestudy@public.io.

A note on Android phones. Samsung, Google Pixel, Xiaomi, Motorola and the rest all arrange their Settings menu slightly differently. Rather than describe a menu that might not match yours, we give you the name of the setting. Open Settings, tap the search box or magnifying glass at the top, and type the name. It will find it whatever your phone.

Not your phones? Route A: iPhone, managed from your iPhone or iPad or Route B: iPhone, set up on your child's phone.

The settings we're asking you to apply

Block everything, then allow back a short list of apps and a short list of websites. You don't need to set limits app by app.

If your child needs an app or a site that isn't here, email smartphonestudy@public.io. We'll answer within five working days: either it goes on the list for everyone, or we tell you why not. Parents built this list and it's still changing.

Steps

  1. Get the Family Link app

    • 2 minutes
    • On your phone
    1. Open the Play Store (Android) or the App Store (iPhone).
    2. Search for Family Link and install it.
    3. Open it and sign in with your own Google Account (often ending in @gmail.com).

  2. Add your child's Google Account

    • 10 minutes
    • On your phone, in Family Link

    Once you've signed in, Family Link asks whether your child has a Google Account.

    1. If they don't have one, choose No and follow the prompts to create one: their name, date of birth, a Gmail address and a password.
      • Check the date of birth is correct. Google uses your child's age to decide which protections apply. A wrong birth year quietly switches off protections you think you have.
      • Write down the new address and password. You'll need them on your child's phone in the next step.
    2. If they already have one, choose Yes and follow the prompts. Check the date of birth on their account is correct too.
    3. After you set the password, read what Google shows you and tap to agree.
    4. Google then checks it's you. You may get a code by text message, and you may be asked for a card's details to confirm you're over 18. You won't be charged.
    5. Family Link shows you what it can do. Tap through to the end.
    6. At Choose settings for your child, choose fewer steps. You'll make the study's settings later in this guide.
    7. When asked about personalising your data, you can tap Reject all.

    You'll then reach Family Link's main screen.

  3. Link your child's phone

    • 10 minutes
    • On your child's phone

    Before you start, check the accounts on your child's phone. The only Google Account on it must be your child's. If your own Google Account is signed in on their phone, remove it first (search Settings for Accounts), or set-up won't let you continue.

    1. On your child's phone, open Settings and tap Google (on some phones: Google services). You don't need anything called All services.
    2. Tap Parental controls. It's under Kids & family (on Samsung phones: Children and family).
    3. Tap Get started, choose Child or teen, then choose your child's account.
    4. When asked for a parent, sign in with your own Google Account. This only confirms it's you.
    5. If asked, set a parental controls PIN: four digits your child doesn't know. Write it down with your other codes, and don't let your child see you type it.
    6. You'll be asked about lots of other settings along the way. Go straight through: accepting them all or saying no to them all are both fine, because you'll make the study's settings next.
    7. Your child enters their own password and taps Agree.
    8. On a Samsung phone, you may also be asked to set up parental controls with a Samsung account. If so:
      • Sign in on their phone with your own Samsung account. If you don't have one, you can create one there, even if your own phone isn't a Samsung.
      • Go to Family → Invite new members → Create child account, and use your child's Google (Gmail) address.
      • Your Samsung account can stay on their phone. Your Google Account must not.

    That's the link made. From now on you manage everything from Family Link on your phone, which now shows your child's phone.

    Can't find Parental controls? Search Settings for parental controls.

  4. Allow only the apps on the list

    • 10 minutes
    • On your phone, in Family Link
    1. Open Family Link and tap Screen time. You don't need to go into Controls.
      • If it asks you to Add device, your child's phone isn't linked yet. Follow the instructions it shows: they're the same as in Link your child's phone.
      • Otherwise you'll see your child's phone, shown by its model name (for example SM-S901B).
    2. Under Schedules there are two options, Downtime and School time. Turn on Downtime.
    3. Tap Weekly schedule → choose a day → Start 12:00 AM, End 11:59 PM → Apply to all days of the week.
    4. Tap Allowed apps. There's no switch to allow them all at once, so go through the apps on the list one at a time and set each one to Unlimited time.

    To block one app outright rather than by schedule: Screen time → Time limits → tap the app → turn Allowed off. Some system apps can't be blocked.

  5. Allow only the websites they need

    • 5 minutes
    • On your phone, in Family Link

    Blocking an app doesn't block its website. This step makes the web work the same way as the apps: only what's on the list.

    1. In Family Link, go to Controls → Google Chrome and Web.
    2. Choose Only allow approved sites.
    3. Tap Approved sites and add each site on the list. Use the main web address only, such as bbc.co.uk. Family Link won't accept a page within a site, such as bbc.co.uk/bitesize.
    4. If other browsers aren't already blocked, block them: Screen time → Time limits → tap each browser → turn Allowed off.
    If a homework site won't load, don't switch the filter off. Email smartphonestudy@public.io and we'll add it to the shared list.

  6. Lock the settings

    • 3 minutes
    • On your phone, in Family Link
    1. In Family Link, go to Controls → Google Play.
    2. Under download approvals, choose All content, so nothing new can be installed without your approval.

  7. Check it worked

    • 2 minutes
    • On your phone
    1. In Family Link, open your child's profile.
    2. If it shows their phone and recent activity, the link is live.
    3. If it shows nothing after a few hours, check the phone is switched on, connected, and signed into the supervised account.

That's it. Thank you!

In about a week, we'll ask you to share a screenshot of your child's screen time.

Optional: time caps on apps on the list

This isn't part of what we're asking. Skip it if you're happy as things stand.

The list works by exempting apps from limits, so an app on the list will ignore a time limit you set on it, on both iPhone and Android. If you want a cap on one of them, email smartphonestudy@public.io and we'll sort out the set-up for your phone.
